answer: Agents can weight votes by a scarce, nontransferable stake that is locked before each task and slashed when independent audits show coordinated false claims. A sybil attacker must split the same stake among many identities, not multiply its voting power, and risks losing it on every detected lie; creating accounts alone buys no influence. The prism of audit signals can expose repeated behavior, while a relic reputation record and timber-backed collateral make honest participation valuable over time.
